micro_protocol: Breast: Microscopic description; In the presented histological specimens, there is a fibroepithelial tumor without a clear boundary, with a hypercellular stroma and numerous ducts, some of which show leaf-like stromal projections. The epithelium is without atypia, with squamous metaplasia in many ducts. The stroma is spindle cell, with plump nuclei, monomorphic, with 9 mitoses/1 mm². Frequent squamous metaplasia is observed within the tumor ducts. Several foci of completely represented squamous nests with microgranules of keratohyalin and rare mitoses were identified at the periphery of the tumor. Immunohistochemical (IHC) study was performed. A layer of myoepithelial cells with expression of Cytokeratin 14 and p63 7JUL was identified around all ducts; these markers are negative in the spindle cell component, as is MCK (AE1/AE3).IHC preparations show ER and PR expression in epithelial cells and rarely in the stroma, CK7 expression in the epithelium, and SMA expression in myoepithelium. CK5/6 and p63 are expressed in myoepithelium. HER2 expression was not detected. Ki67 index is high in the stroma.

Nuclear marker expression in less than 1% of cells, with moderate to strong expression intensity (total score 3-4) is considered a positive result. micro_protocol: Breast: Microscopic description: Six histological specimens were provided. Specimens 45987-94/19 show breast tissue with areas suspicious for unspecified carcinoma G1 (1+2+1=4 according to NGS) with a largest dimension of 6mm. Other specimens show foci of dilated ducts with epithelial cell proliferation and mild atypia, suspicious for carcinoma in situ. Also present in the specimens are foci of adenosis and fibrosis. To clarify the presence of invasive carcinoma, new specimens were prepared from four paraffin blocks. 52041-1B-1. Breast tissue with stromal fibrosis and a focus of adenosis. Immunohistochemical staining was performed to confirm the presence of myoepithelium – a layer of myoepithelium with expression of Cytokeratin 14, Calponin-1 (EP798Y) (Calp-1 (EP798Y)) surrounds the foci of adenosis. 52041-2B-1. Breast tissue with foci of stromal fibrosis. 52041-3B-1, 52041-4B-1. Breast tissue with stromal fibrosis and numerous cystically dilated ducts. Some ducts show columnar epithelial proliferation with hyperchromatic nuclei, and some show solid epithelial proliferation consisting of relatively monomorphic cells with round nuclei. Immunohistochemical staining was performed to confirm the presence of myoepithelium – a layer of myoepithelium with expression of Cytokeratin 14, Calponin-1 (EP798Y) (Calp-1 (EP798Y)) surrounds the foci of adenosis; however, the expression of CK14 is absent in the epithelial cells of the ducts with solid proliferation. In some ducts, there are calcifications. The nuclei of the epithelium in the proliferation zone show pronounced diffuse expression of ER (6F11). Expression of CK14 is absent around areas suspicious for invasion, confirming the presence of carcinoma. Weak ER expression (2+1=3 according to Allred) was detected in the atypical glands. Diagnostic material in the block was exhausted during Calponin staining.

conclusion: Invasive breast carcinoma, Grade III according to the Nottingham system (see comment).

diff_diagnostic: Due to the specific morphological characteristics of the tumor (well-defined node with a predominantly solid, as well as cribriform growth pattern from tumor cells with mild to moderate nuclear pleomorphism with low mitotic activity, with inconspicuous fibrovacular stalks), solid papillary carcinoma with an invasive component cannot be excluded. Therefore, immunohistochemical testing (2 antibodies: Synaptophysin, Chromogranin A) is recommended. Staging of the tumor according to TNM is also difficult due to the difficulty in objectively assessing the extent of the invasive component; therefore, immunohistochemical testing on 4 blocks (8 antibodies: Calponin (2), CK14 (2)) is recommended. Evaluation of resection margins is difficult because in the primary material of sector resection, the stained margin partially runs through tumor elements. Furthermore, in the additionally submitted lateral margins, the true surgical margin is not marked, and in areas of coagulation and areas stained with dye, foci suspicious for tumor growth are identified - to objectify this, immunohistochemical testing on 3 blocks (6 antibodies: Calponin (3), CK14 (3)) is recommended. Considering the uncertainty in the extent of the invasive component of the carcinoma, assessment of the surrogate molecular-genetic subtype is recommended after clarification of the size of the invasive carcinoma based on immunohistochemical study results.
